facts.text: The organization operates 2 sites: Sample: Hospital 1 and Sample: Hospital 2, with about 1200 staff.
Assessment scope: Two hospitals, HIS, PACS, LIS, ERP, Microsoft 365. Fictional example data.
HIS supports Patient registration, orders, billing, Criticality A, tolerable downtime Under 4 hours.
PACS supports Medical imaging, Criticality A, tolerable downtime 4 hours to 1 day.
Microsoft 365 supports Email, Teams, files, Criticality A, tolerable downtime 4 hours to 1 day.
Active Directory and network core supports Logon and connectivity for all systems, Criticality A, tolerable downtime Under 4 hours.
7 systems listed: 4 Criticality A, 3 B, 0 C.
Origin: 3 standard commercial software, 2 customized commercial software, 1 SaaS and 1 outsourced custom build.
Hosting: 3 on-premises data center, 2 vendor-hosted, 1 SaaS and 1 public cloud.

Department interviews found 3 systems or apps not on the IT list: Sample: diet order sheet on Google Sheets (Sample: Food and Beverage), Sample: Canva (Sample: Marketing and PR) and Sample: Facebook Business Suite (Sample: Marketing and PR).
Primary data center: Sample: server room at Hospital 1.
Disaster recovery site: Yes, not tested.
Network segmentation: Partly segmented.
Staff remote access: VPN without MFA.
Workstations: 900.
Workstations on end-of-life operating systems: 5 to 20 percent.
Networked medical devices and OT: 150.
Medical device and OT network placement: Shared with the corporate network.
Backup architecture: Online copy only.
1 system directly exposed to the internet: Hospital website.
Authentication: Local accounts in the application (4), Directory, such as Active Directory or LDAP (2) and Single sign-on through SAML or OpenID Connect (1).
Multi-factor authentication (MFA): None (6) and Administrators and remote access only (1).
Administrator accounts: Named but too many (3), Shared or generic (3) and Named and limited (1).
Shared workstations in operational areas: Yes.

Departments reporting shared accounts or passwords: Sample: Outpatient Nursing (Named accounts, but passwords are shared sometimes), Sample: Food and Beverage (Shared account for the team or shift) and Sample: Marketing and PR (Named accounts, but passwords are shared sometimes).
Shared computers stay logged in all shift in Sample: Outpatient Nursing and Sample: Food and Beverage.
Firewall: Sample: next-generation firewall, coverage full, operated by in-house, in use.
Endpoint detection and response (EDR): Sample: EDR agent, coverage partial, operated by in-house, in use.
Antivirus: Sample: antivirus, coverage full, operated by in-house, in use.
Email security: Sample: Microsoft 365 email filtering, coverage full, operated by vendor, in use.
Central logging or SIEM: Sample: syslog server, coverage partial, operated by nobody, in use.
MFA provider: Sample: Microsoft Entra ID MFA, coverage partial, operated by in-house, in use.
Vulnerability scanning: Sample: vulnerability scanner license, coverage none, operated by nobody, bought, not deployed.
Privileged access management (PAM): no product named, coverage none, operated by nobody, planned.
Backup: Sample: backup software, coverage partial, operated by in-house, in use.
4 vendors with system or data access: Software vendor (2), Medical device vendor (1) and Cloud or SaaS provider (1).
3 vendors connect remotely: Sample HIS vendor, Sample PACS vendor and Sample web agency.
Criticality A vendors: Sample HIS vendor, Sample PACS vendor and Sample cloud provider.
Sensitive personal data sits in 3 systems: HIS, PACS and LIS.
Personal data sits in 3 more systems: ERP, Microsoft 365 and Hospital website.
Vendors with access to sensitive personal data: Sample HIS vendor and Sample PACS vendor.

Departments that move work data through personal channels: Sample: Outpatient Nursing (Personal LINE or other chat app, Photos on personal phones), Sample: Food and Beverage (Personal LINE or other chat app), Sample: Finance (USB drive) and Sample: Marketing and PR (Personal cloud storage, Personal email).
IT headcount: 25.
Security role: Part-time, held by an IT role.
Outsourced IT functions: Application support.
Security training within 12 months: 1 of 4 departments interviewed.
C3 Authentication: 3 Good, 4 Weak, 0 Poor, 0 Unknown of 7 systems answered (Criticality A: 2 Good of 4).
C4 Multi-factor authentication (MFA): 0 Good, 1 Weak, 6 Poor, 0 Unknown of 7 systems answered (Criticality A: 0 Good of 4).
C5 Administrator accounts: 1 Good, 3 Weak, 3 Poor, 0 Unknown of 7 systems answered (Criticality A: 0 Good of 4).
C6 Internet exposure: 5 Good, 0 Weak, 1 Poor, 0 Unknown of 6 systems answered (Criticality A: 3 Good of 3).
C7 Vendor remote access: 0 Good, 2 Weak, 3 Poor, 0 Unknown of 5 systems answered (Criticality A: 0 Good of 2).
C8 Platform support and patching: 0 Good, 3 Weak, 2 Poor, 1 Unknown of 6 systems answered (Criticality A: 0 Good of 3).
C9 Backup: 1 Good, 4 Weak, 1 Poor, 1 Unknown of 7 systems answered (Criticality A: 1 Good of 4).
Assessment date 2026-10-05. 7 systems listed, 4 sampled.
6 profile answers recorded as Unknown.
Technical observations (vulnerabilities): 1 High. Details stay in the Technical Observation Register.
4 departments interviewed in S2C. 6 answers conflict with what IT stated.
Staff do not know how to report a suspicious event in Sample: Food and Beverage.
2025-03-12: account compromise or phishing affecting Microsoft 365. Sample: one mailbox sent phishing email to patients for two hours.
Sample: PACS replacement: PACS, target 2027-03-31, contracted, within 12 months.
Sample: HIS major version upgrade: HIS, target 2028-01-31, planned.
Internal audit on 2025-11-20 by Sample: CMC Internal Audit: 6 findings open, 2 closed.
Penetration test on 2024-08-15 by Sample: external testing firm, hospital website: 4 findings open, 1 closed.
